EBITDA beat-and-raise habit (Q2 $2.98m vs $2.6-2.7m guide; FY floor raised $11.8m -> $12.0m -> $12.7m) against FY revenue arithmetic that needs Q4 to grow ~5% sequentially at the guide midpoint (last year's Q4 grew ~2.4%), so p_up 52 on an abs move of 11 (median 7.5, max 37.5, thin ~$0.6m/day, Q4 guide new) gives +0.44; impact_sum +0.3 agrees in sign and size.
bar: Q3 revenue $10.94m / adj EPS $0.27 (MarketBeat consensus, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/audioeye-nasdaqaeye-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-13/), which sits on the company guide midpoint: revenue $10.85-11.05m, adj EBITDA $3.4-3.6m, adj EPS $0.26-0.28; FY revenue $43.5-44.0m, FY adj EBITDA >= $12.7m, FY adj EPS >= $0.98 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926095913/aeye-20260813xex99d1.htm). Older MarketBeat/Benzinga figures ($11.2m / $11.13m revenue, $0.23 EPS) were pre-guide and are disowned.
positioning_check: Short interest 263,802 shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, 2.38 days to cover (338,568 / 1.40 at 09-15) per https://equibles.com/stocks/aeye/shortinterest; against ~12.57m shares outstanding (10-Q cover) that is ~2% of shares, not crowded. No usable option chain (ATM spread 108% of mid, OI 73), so no skew; put/call OI 0.59 on a meaningless chain. Run-up +14.8% 5d / +17.7% 20d into the print, most of it after the 2026-10-20 $15m buyback release; still -48% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Adj. EBITDA has beaten guidance and the FY floor has been raised at every print this year: Q2 adj EBITDA $2.98m against a $2.6-2.7m guide (~10% over the top), FY floor $11.8m (Mar) -> >= $12.0m (May) -> >= $12.7m (Aug); H1 = $5.38m, so the FY floor with Q3 at the $3.5m guide midpoint needs only Q4 ~$3.8m, which matches the stated >$15m year-end run-rate; a repeat Q3 beat (~$3.8-3.9m vs the $3.4-3.6m guide and $0.27 EPS consensus) would mechanically push the FY floor toward ~$13m+.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-13 (Q2 EBITDA beat + FY EBITDA raise): +37.5%. 2026-05-12 (FY EBITDA floor raised to $12m): -5.3%. 2026-03-05 (first 2026 guide): -22.4%. Mixed, but the largest up-move in the history came on exactly this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS ($0.27) sits on the guide midpoint, not above it, although the company beat the top of its Q2 EBITDA and EPS guide ($0.23 vs $0.21-0.22). If the beat habit were priced the bar would sit at or above the top of the range. The +17.7% 20-day run-up partly prices a good print, which is why this is sized well under the Aug reaction.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm) shows the May floor raise; FY2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/592487/audioeye-reports-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) shows the original ~$11.8m. Same issuer, different documents. CEO's 2026-10-20 buyback quote ('expect to generate meaningful cash over the next year as operating leverage continues to increase') points the same way.

findings.finding: FY revenue guide arithmetic is tight at the midpoint: H1 revenue $21.269m (10-Q), FY guide $43.5-44.0m, Q3 guide midpoint $10.95m, so Q4 must be $11.28-11.78m (midpoint $11.53m, +5.3% sequential); last year Q4 2025 grew ~2.4% sequentially ($10.5m vs ~$10.25m) and ARR added only ~$1.1-1.2m a quarter in 2026 ($40.0m -> $41.2m -> $42.3m), which on the same Q4 step lands FY near $43.4-43.65m, i.e. at or just under the low end unless Q3 prints at the top of its range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY revenue range has been narrowed twice with the $43.75m midpoint held (Mar $43-44.5m, May $43.25-44.25m, Aug $43.5-44.0m); Aug the Q3 revenue guide came in under the then-$11.1-11.2m consensus and the stock still rose 37.5% on EBITDA. Revenue-line misses have not been the driver of past moves as far as the releases show.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 implied number is never printed by the company and the visible consensus is a Q3 number on the guide midpoint; if the market had done the arithmetic, the FY revenue consensus would sit near the low end ($43.5m) rather than the midpoint and a trim would be a non-event. Inference from primary numbers, not a disclosed shortfall, hence small.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 sequential step from the FY2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/592487/audioeye-reports-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results); ARR path from the Q1 and Q2 releases. Counterweight: CEO said in May he expects sequential revenue growth to accelerate through the year (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm), which is why this is not larger.

findings.finding: Growth is now entirely the partner channel and concentrated: Q2 Enterprise revenue $4.472m vs $4.458m a year earlier (+0.3%), Partner & Marketplace $6.244m vs $5.399m (+16%); two customers were 10% and 13% of Q2 revenue (23% combined), and in Q1 'one partner's realignment of their own customers' removed ~4,000 customers. Net of the rest: the partner channel (58% of revenue, ~59% of ARR) growing 16% carries the whole company, so a flat enterprise line only hurts if a large partner wobbles.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release in the baseline set turned visibly on channel mix; the Q1 customer-count drop (2026-05-12) coincided with -5.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The channel split and the 23% concentration sit in the 10-Q notes, not in the press release that the wires carried; the release only says growth came from Partner & Marketplace. Public since August and followed by a +37.5% day, so weight is small.
findings.independence: Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm) for the partner realignment; same issuer.

findings.finding: The $15m buyback announced 2026-10-20 (about 15% of a ~$100m market cap: 12.57m shares x ~$8; cash $8.7m and term loan $16.8m at June 30) is wider than what the lender permits: the 2026-09-18 Fourth Loan Modification with Western Alliance caps permitted buybacks at $7.0m in aggregate across FY2025-2027 ($2.0m a year from 2028), and ~$0.5m was already used in H1 2026, so the call will likely describe a pace well under the headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback-on-print in the baseline; the stock is +14.8% over the 5 sessions around the announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: The buyback headline went out by wire; the lender cap sits only in a separate 8-K a month earlier and is not cited in any coverage found. If priced, the run-up into the print would not be concentrated after the $15m headline. Covenant arithmetic, and the same amendment loosened the cap (lender cooperative), so sized small.
findings.independence: Buyback 8-K and release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1362190/000110465926117191/tm2627892d1_8k.htm (2026-10-20). Share and balance-sheet figures from the 10-Q. Shares a document with the litigation finding below.

findings.finding: Litigation spending is a live drag on cash quality: Q2 G&A rose 'primarily' on litigation expense (no figure disclosed), and the same 2026-09-18 loan amendment lets litigation expense of up to $5.0m TTM through 2026 ($3.0m in 2027) be added back to covenant EBITDA, against ~$10m TTM adj EBITDA; management said in August that falling litigation expense would drive 'meaningful' H2 free cash flow, and Q3 is the first test.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline set turned on litigation or FCF as far as the releases show.
findings.why_not_priced: The add-back size is in a credit-agreement amendment, not in any release; if the market expected litigation to stay large it would not be paying for the 'meaningful FCF' promise with a +17.7% run-up. Covenant headroom is ample (debt/EBITDA ~1.7x vs 2.5x test), so this is a quality-of-cash question, not distress (lesson 4 answered: no covenant pressure).
findings.independence: 10-Q MD&A on G&A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1362190/000110465926096032/aeye-20260630x10q.htm). Shares the 2026-09-18 8-K with the buyback finding; different facts in it.

findings.finding: Demand backdrop: website/digital accessibility lawsuits were tracking to exceed 6,000 in 2026 (~+20% on 2025's ~4,928) and federal ADA Title III filings were 5,006 in H1 2026, the highest first half since 2021, while DOJ's Title II deadline moved to 2027-04-26 (rule intact, WCAG 2.1 AA unchanged), which management tied to partner penetration ahead of 2027 deadlines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 Title II delay preceded the 2026-04-27 print (-1.8%); no clean read.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with; the +17.7% 20-day run-up after the buyback headline already prices part of a good EBITDA print, which is why the beat-and-raise finding is sized at a fraction of the August reaction and p_up sits only just above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the 2026-09-18 amendment loosens covenants with ~1.7x leverage vs a 2.5x test, so the litigation add-back finding went from -0.3 to -0.2 and is framed as cash quality, not distress.
'Covenant arithmetic has not paid': the buyback-cap finding went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest) plus public-since-August: the enterprise-flat/concentration finding went from -0.5 to -0.3, because the 58% partner channel grew 16%.
Lesson 2/5 (guidance line, but inference rather than a disclosed number): the FY revenue arithmetic finding went from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 8 (thin name, Q4 guide new): abs_move_pct up from 10 to 11; p_up from 51 to 52 after the negatives shrank.
EBITDA beat-and-raise (+1.5) and the lawsuit proxy (+0.3) left standing.
